title: Virginia: history overview
d: Virginia: the Old Dominion, admitted 1788 (10th); capital Richmond.
definition: Virginia: the Old Dominion, admitted 1788 (10th); capital Richmond.
description: Virginia — "Old Dominion" — entered the Union 1788 (10th). Its capital is Richmond and its largest city is Virginia Beach. Jamestown 1607; 8 presidents. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Virginia achieved statehood 1788 (10th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Revolution; Civil War capital. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Virginia its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Virginia went from territory to state.
definition: How Virginia went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Virginia: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Government; tech; history. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Virginia's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Richmond
d: Richmond is the capital of Virginia.
definition: Richmond is the capital of Virginia.
description: Richmond has been the seat of Virginia government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Virginia's largest is Virginia Beach — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Old Dominion
description: The nickname "Old Dominion" captures how Virginia sees itself — and how America sees it. Eight U.S. presidents were born in Virginia. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Sic semper tyrannis (Thus always to tyrants)."

title: Motto: Sic semper tyrannis (Thus always to tyrants)
t: Motto: Sic semper tyrannis (Thus always to tyrants)
d: The state motto of Virginia is "Sic semper tyrannis (Thus always to tyrants)."
definition: The state motto of Virginia is "Sic semper tyrannis (Thus always to tyrants)."
description: The motto "Sic semper tyrannis (Thus always to tyrants)" is Virginia's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Virtus standing on tyrant on blue. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
